## Watch vendor sub-processor pages for changes

Your vendors publish the list of companies they pass your data to, and are supposed to tell you when it changes. This checks the pages rather than trusting the notice.

### How it works
A form adds a vendor, its public sub-processor page and the countries you approved. Check Now or the Monday schedule fetches each page, strips the markup and reduces it to a set of entry lines. The comparison is a line by line set difference against the register: what appeared, what disappeared. Nothing else is parsed, so a redesign does not break it.

Two failures are treated as failures rather than good news. A page that cannot be read is UNREACHABLE and the register is untouched, because an outage must never read as "no changes". A page returning far fewer entries than the register holds is SUSPECT, and removals are held back, so a login wall cannot quietly empty it.

One Groq call then reads only the lines that appeared and names the company and country from the line itself. A country not written in the line is discarded. It never creates, removes or re-grades a finding.

Runs, findings and the register are stored. A new line naming an unapproved country raises ALERT. Anything not quiet goes to Discord; a quiet week gets a short summary.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the model node and a Discord webhook credential to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once, then add your first vendor with the form.
3. Run Check Now. The first check records a baseline and reports no changes.

### Customization tips
Set Watch Policy holds the country words, the shrink ratio and the entry cap. Add the countries you care about.

## 1. Create the tables (run once)
Four tables with typed columns, reused if the names exist. Nothing is seeded: the vendors are yours and you add them with the form. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Add a vendor to watch
The [form](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger/) takes the vendor, its public list page and your approved countries. A page address that is not a web address is saved but left disabled, with the reason.

## 3. Start a check
Check Now or the Monday [schedule](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/). Set Watch Policy holds the country words, the shrink ratio and the entry cap. Only enabled vendors with a page are queued.

## 4. Fetch and reduce
The [HTTP node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.httprequest/) fetches the page and never throws. Markup is stripped and the page becomes a set of entry lines plus a hash. A failed fetch is marked unreachable here.

## 5. Compare, then describe
A set difference against the register: an unreachable page is skipped untouched and a shrunken page keeps its removals held back. The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) then names the company and country from an added line only.

## 6. Record
One row per run in sub_runs, one per finding in sub_findings, one per entry in sub_register with first and last seen. A run that found nothing still writes a row.

## 7. Escalate
An unapproved country, a change, or an unreadable page goes through the [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/) webhook; a quiet run posts a short summary instead. Swap Discord for Slack or Gmail.
